name: Mario Draghi
role: Italian prime minister (2021–2022) and European Central Bank president (2011–2019)
summary: Draghi advocates deeper European integration, competitive markets supported by social protection, strategic investment and a rapid clean-energy transition. His later proposals combine greater European defense capacity with continued transatlantic cooperation, and favor pragmatic institutional reform over blanket protectionism or economic isolation.

universal-healthcare.rationale: He proposes strengthening the national health service and community facilities to make essential care effectively accessible.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He favors continental competition and market signals, alongside public coordination where markets cannot provide strategic capacity.

unions-good.rationale: He calls for full union involvement in the social pact and recognizes their collective contracts as central to the system.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He calls for substantially simpler business and data rules, while defending effective financial oversight; his position differentiates regulatory purposes and burdens.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He calls for supporting cultural activities because losing that heritage would damage Italy’s identity as well as its economy.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He advocates stronger multilateral institutions and common enforcement to sustain open markets and regulate cross-border risks.

free-trade.rationale: He defends gains from further trade liberalization but says openness alone cannot resolve Europe’s strategic and productive weaknesses.

nation-first.rationale: He holds that true sovereignty comes only by working together and that returning to national sovereignty would expose Europe to the great powers.

open-borders.rationale: His programme calls for a European returns policy for people without protection rights alongside respect for refugees.

limit-growth.rationale: He insists Europe must raise productivity and growth while achieving decarbonization and sustaining social inclusion.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He calls for coordinated decarbonization and public investment toward climate neutrality, treating the transition as indispensable.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He calls for faster investment in clean baseload generation, explicitly including nuclear power.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: He permits selective defensive tariffs against subsidized foreign competition, while rejecting systematic protection and requiring attention to consumer costs.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He advocates European coordination of strategic industrial investment and public funding of innovation, infrastructure and defense.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: He argues for preserving independent central banks and their monetary-policy instruments rather than dismantling them.

democracy-best.rationale: He presents democracy as a founding value to defend against authoritarian models and the Union as a collective defence of democracy; he does not address voters choosing badly.

separate-church-state.rationale: Responding to Vatican objections, he stresses Italy’s secular character and parliament’s freedom to debate legislation.

accelerate-technology.rationale: He urges rapid AI deployment and a pause in high-risk AI rules until their drawbacks are better understood.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He rejects ideological rigidity in economic policy and favors experiments judged by visible results and democratic accountability.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: His later crisis prescription accepts major public-debt increases to prevent depression, qualifying his earlier support for consolidation.

class-collaboration.rationale: He seeks a social pact involving unions and the government to address wages, insecurity and living costs.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: He urges support for museums, theaters and the arts and investment in inherited cultural assets, rather than allowing their disappearance.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He holds that the state should run industrial policy and social protection, and says the era of shrinking state powers is over, which contradicts a defence-only state.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He said national unity was the best guarantee of this government's democratic legitimacy and that a prime minister who never faced voters needs the broadest parliamentary support.

trade-surplus.rationale: The strategy explicitly rejects pursuing competitiveness through trade surpluses or shielding national champions from competition.

separated-powers.rationale: He defends independent monetary institutions operating under legislative mandates and being held accountable by elected legislators.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He called for a social agenda that starts from the weakest and for tax relief beginning with the lowest wages.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He explicitly proposes pragmatic federalism through common European institutions with real authority and democratic endorsement.

clerical-rule.rationale: He rejects treating Italy as a confessional state and defends parliamentary autonomy against Vatican intervention.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He says stronger European defense should reinforce NATO and the transatlantic relationship rather than dissolve them.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: At the UN he called for more ambitious support for poorer countries, tripled Italy's vaccine donations and backed new IMF reserves and debt restructuring.

central-bank-independence.rationale: He defends monetary authorities’ freedom from political and fiscal dominance, within legislatively defined mandates and public accountability.

collective-defense.rationale: He demands clear, binding European mutual-defense commitments and operational plans for responding when a member is attacked.

flat-income-tax.rationale: He explicitly requires tax reform to preserve progressivity while simplifying and reducing the overall burden.

common-currency.rationale: He defends the euro as a means for participating countries to regain effective monetary sovereignty together.

no-bailouts.rationale: During the pandemic he explicitly urged public guarantees and absorption of business losses to preserve employment and productive capacity.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: He points to constitutional judicial review as a guarantee when parliament debates contested legislation.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: He says Europe cannot reshore every critical technology and needs trusted partners and secure international supply chains.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The report recommends strengthening the EU investment screening mechanism and coordinating FDI decisions to protect strategic sectors.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: He calls for using both public and private facilities to deliver the vaccination campaign, within the national public-health response.

social-market-economy.rationale: His strategy combines open competitive markets with strong public services, social protection and support for workers through economic transitions.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He calls for rebuilding European defense capabilities, procurement and research to make collective defense credible.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He explicitly anchors Italy in the Atlantic alliance and proposes making European capabilities a stronger component of that partnership.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: He argued that ECB bond-buying needs government conditionality, otherwise it would not be effective, and welcomed the Greek parliament's approval of austerity measures.

future-generations.rationale: He explicitly links environmental policy to leaving later generations a healthy planet.

collective-bargaining.rationale: As prime minister (2021-22) he called collective contracts a pillar and strength of Italy's wage system; this later position outweighs his 2014 call for more firm-level agreements, so +1.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: He conditions systematic common borrowing on stronger fiscal rules and sustainable national debt paths, while supporting joint investment debt.

close-ties-china.rationale: He stresses the transatlantic bond and warns that China treats Europe as unequal and uses dependence on rare earths, and the report seeks to cut reliance on China.

no-business-privileges.rationale: He favors comprehensive tax reform partly to prevent pressure groups obtaining measures tailored to their own advantage.

notes:
No inferred answers. Reviewed downloaded full texts of the 2021 programme, 2024 competitiveness strategy and 2026 Aachen address across all statement themes. The 2020 pandemic proposal and later investment programme qualify the fiscal consolidation arguments of 2012. Citizenship income is means-tested support, not evidence for an unconditional universal basic income. His secular-state response expressly declined to decide the merits of the Zan bill, so it is not coded as support for every provision of that bill. General commitments to rights, technology and democracy do not answer their more specific quiz variants. Expert preparation of tax reform is not treated as a general demand to subordinate voters to experts. Support for means-tested income aid does not settle the broader dependency-and-welfare-cuts statement. The proposed wage floor is recorded through the explicit collective-bargaining position; no numerical call for a substantial minimum-wage increase was established.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 9 answers taken from it, 16 agreed, 1 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second pass from sources not used in the first audit: ECB speeches, hearings and press conference 2012-2019, Bank of Italy final considerations, the 2022 Parliament and Senate speeches, UN speeches 2021-22, Rimini 2025, and the 2024 report. Themes searched: economy, government, society, world, liberty, culture, ecology, technology, means, globalism. Statements as ECB President speak for the institution's mandate; where his personal speeches differ they were preferred. Most social, liberty, culture and government statements have no recorded personal position in the texts read. His 2014 Jackson Hole speech favours firm-level wage agreements, which qualifies the collective-bargaining answer. Not opened: Rimini 2020 text (page 404; mirror behind Cloudflare), Britannica (Cloudflare), Oviedo 2025 PDF (timeout).
